query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing chromium (Cr) into an equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy to form a FeCoNiCr system increases its coercivity relative to previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic FeCoNi alloy with an fcc structure that exhibits high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Addition of chromium (Cr) to form a FeCoNiCr high-entropy alloy.
generation.conditions: The alloy must be synthesized with an equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition of Fe, Co, Ni, and Cr to ensure a configurational entropy of at least 1.0R, and processed under conditions (e.g., melting and annealing) that maintain a single-phase fcc structure.
generation.structural_mediator: The introduction of Cr increases lattice distortion and modifies the magnetic anisotropy, creating effective pinning sites for domain walls.
generation.mechanism: Cr atoms introduced into the FeCoNi lattice generate local lattice distortions and alter exchange interactions, which enhance domain wall pinning and magnetic anisotropy. This impedes domain wall motion during magnetization reversal, resulting in an increased coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiCr high-entropy alloy will exhibit a higher coercive field compared to the baseline FeCoNi alloy and its derivatives (FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt), while largely retaining its high saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: FeCoNi-based alloys, including those containing Pd or Pt, that show soft ferromagnetic behavior with low coercivity.
generation.boundary: This prediction holds when the alloy maintains an equiatomic composition and a homogeneous single-phase fcc structure. Significant deviations in composition or the emergence of secondary phases may negate the coercivity enhancement.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may vary with processing conditions and precise Cr content within the equiatomic framework.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of high-entropy alloys under controlled conditions: one set with equiatomic FeCoNiCr and a control set with either FeCoNi or FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt compositions. Characterize the phase purity and structure via X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy. Measure their magnetic hysteresis loops using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) to determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: Phase structure and homogeneity via XRD and electron microscopy
Magnetic hysteresis loops to extract coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured coercivity of the FeCoNiCr alloy is not significantly higher (e.g., less than a 10% increase) than that of the control alloys under identical processing and measurement conditions, or if the alloy does not maintain a single-phase fcc structure, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Replacing the heavy 5d element in FeCoNi-based HEAs with iridium (Ir) will increase the coercivity relative to the earlier FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys.
drafts.material_initial_state: An fcc FeCoNi-based alloy with nearly equiatomic composition and high configurational entropy (≥1.0R), originally exhibiting high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
drafts.intervention: Introduce Ir as one of the principal equiatomic components (i.e., form a FeCoNiIr high-entropy alloy) in place of, or in addition to, other heavy 5d elements.
drafts.conditions: The alloy should remain equiatomic and retain an fcc structure; processing conditions (e.g., melting and annealing) must promote homogenous mixing and single-phase formation to ensure high configurational entropy.
drafts.structural_mediator: The incorporation of Ir is expected to influence the microstructure by increasing lattice distortion and encouraging stronger spin–orbit coupling, which in turn enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
drafts.mechanism: Ir has a greater spin–orbit coupling compared to Pd and Pt. By being incorporated at equiatomic levels, its strong spin–orbit interaction will increase the magnetic anisotropy energy barriers that need to be overcome for domain wall motion or magnetization reversal, thereby increasing the coercivity. This effect should persist while maintaining a high saturation magnetization due to the FeCoNi framework.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiIr alloy will exhibit a higher coercive field compared to the soft ferromagnets FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, while still retaining a high saturation magnetization.
drafts.baseline: FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys, which have a similar nearly equiatomic composition and fcc structure but show lower coercivity.
drafts.boundary: The hypothesis applies when the high-entropy alloy is synthesized with equiatomic distribution and processed under conditions that preserve a single-phase fcc structure. Deviations from equiatomic ratios or formation of secondary phases may obscure the coercivity enhancement.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys: one set with Ir (FeCoNiIr) and a control set with Pd and/or Pt (FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt). Confirm the equiatomic composition and fcc structure via x-ray diffraction and electron microscopy. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops using techniques such as vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM) at room temperature to determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.
measurements: Lattice structure and phase purity (XRD, SEM/TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured coercivity of the FeCoNiIr alloy is not significantly greater (e.g., less than a 10% increase) than that of the baseline FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt alloys under identical processing and measurement conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Introducing a near-equiatomic amount of Al and Cr to form a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy that undergoes partial B2 precipitation in an fcc matrix will increase domain-wall pinning and yield higher coercivity compared to FeCoNi-based alloys without these precipitates (such as FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt).
drafts.material_initial_state: A soft ferromagnetic, single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy with a low coercive field.
drafts.intervention: Add Al and Cr in near-equiatomic ratios to FeCoNi (resulting in a FeCoNiCrAl composition) while ensuring a total configurational entropy ≥1.0R, followed by solution annealing and subsequent aging treatment to promote B2 nanoprecipitate formation.
drafts.conditions: Solution anneal at ~1100 °C for several hours to ensure a homogeneous solid solution, water-quench to retain the fcc matrix, and then age at 600–800 °C to form controlled B2 nanoprecipitates.
drafts.structural_mediator: Nanoscale B2 precipitates embedded in an fcc matrix providing strong domain wall pinning sites.
drafts.mechanism: The dispersed B2 second phase interfaces act as barriers to domain wall motion, increasing coercivity without critically reducing the overall magnetic moment.
drafts.predicted_outcome: A significantly higher coercive field (on the order of several times the baseline) relative to soft ferromagnetic FeCoNi-based alloys containing Pt or Pd, while largely preserving high saturation magnetization.
drafts.baseline: Soft-ferromagnetic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys (e.g., FeCoNiPd, FeCoNiPt) that exhibit relatively low coercivity.
drafts.boundary: If the Al content is too high or if the solution treatment/aging steps are not well controlled, the alloy may become brittle, exhibit multi-phase segregation patterns detrimental to magnetic performance, or lose the high-entropy characteristic.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize multiple alloy samples with near-equiatomic FeCoNiCrAl compositions. Perform a solution anneal at ~1100 °C for a fixed duration (e.g., 24 hours) followed by water-quenching. Age each sample at different temperatures (600, 700, 800 °C) and times (2, 4, 8 hours).
measurements: Magnetic hysteresis loops for coercive field (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms)
Microstructure and precipitate characterization via XRD, SEM, and TEM
Elemental distribution using EDS or similar technique
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aged FeCoNiCrAl samples do not show any B2 precipitate formation or if their coercivity does not exceed that of the FeCoNi baseline or previously studied FeCoNiPd/Pt alloys, then this hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.structural_mediator: The addition of Cr introduces lattice distortion and modifies the magnetic anisotropy of the alloy.

drafts.predicted_outcome: The coercivity of the FeCoNiCr high-entropy alloy will be higher than that of FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, and FeCoNiPt, while still exhibiting soft ferromagnetic behavior.
drafts.baseline: The coercivity of the FeCoNi alloy and its derivatives FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, which exhibit soft ferromagnetism.
drafts.boundary: The hypothesis applies to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with equiatomic or near-equiatomic compositions and a single-phase fcc structure. Deviations from these conditions, such as phase separation or significant compositional imbalance, may invalidate the prediction.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a FeCoNiCr high-entropy alloy with an equiatomic composition and compare its coercivity to that of FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, and FeCoNiPt under identical measurement conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCoNiCr alloy is not higher than that of FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, and FeCoNiPt, or if the alloy does not maintain a single-phase fcc structure, the hypothesis is falsified.
